title: Inverse Approximation Theory for Nonlinear Recurrent Neural Networks

en.text: Recurrent neural networks are one of the most basic tools we reach for when data arrives as a sequence: time series, speech, text, sentiment. They are also famous for one recurring disappointment. When the signal depends on something that happened far in the past, plain RNNs tend to lose the thread. The usual explanation is an optimization story: gradients that vanish or explode as they are propagated back through many time steps, making long-range dependencies hard to train.

But that explanation leaves a sharper question unanswered. Is the trouble with long-term memory merely a training artifact that a better optimizer might fix, or is it a structural limit of what an RNN can represent at all? The two diagnoses call for very different responses, and telling them apart requires an approximation-theoretic lens rather than an optimization one.

This ICLR 2024 paper settles the question for nonlinear RNNs. It proves an inverse, or Bernstein-type, approximation theorem: if a nonlinear RNN can stably approximate a target sequence relationship, then that target's memory must decay exponentially in time. In other words, the difficulty with long-term dependencies is baked into the RNN hypothesis space, not just the optimizer. The same analysis then points to a cure, a stable reparameterization of the recurrent weights that provably and empirically relaxes the limit.
Authors: Zhong Li (Microsoft Research Asia), Shida Wang and Qianxiao Li (National University of Singapore; Institute for Functional Intelligent Materials).
Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.19190
Two directions in approximation theory

Approximation theory offers two complementary kinds of statement. A forward, or Jackson-type, theorem tells you how well a model can approximate a target that is sufficiently regular. An inverse, or Bernstein-type, theorem runs the other way: it assumes a target can be approximated efficiently and then deduces what regularity the target must have had in the first place. Most approximation results in machine learning are forward theorems, which is why they rarely expose an architecture's true ceiling. Inverse theorems are exactly the tool for that job.

There was already a precedent. Earlier work proved a Bernstein-type result for linear RNNs, showing that any linear target they can efficiently approximate must have exponentially decaying memory, a phenomenon dubbed the curse of memory. The open and pressing question was whether nonlinearity, which greatly enlarges a model's capacity, would break the curse. Intuitively, more expressive models should be able to hold on to more of the past. This paper asks whether that intuition survives contact with a rigorous inverse theorem.
Two tools: a memory function and stable approximation

The analysis rests on two ingredients. The first is a memory function generalized from the linear setting to arbitrary nonlinear functional sequences. It probes the model with Heaviside step inputs and measures how strongly the output at time t still responds to the input, through the derivative of that response. Crucially, this memory function is not just an abstract definition: it can be numerically queried from a trained model, so you can actually plot how a network's memory decays.

The second ingredient is a notion of stable approximation. Gradient-based training only works if small changes to the parameters cause small changes to the model, so the authors define the perturbation error at hidden dimension m as the worst-case output error when the parameters are perturbed within a ball of radius beta. A target is stably approximated if that perturbation error stays continuous up to some positive radius, called the stability radius. This is a mild, optimization-friendly requirement, and it is the hinge of the whole argument.

Figure 1 makes the good case concrete. For a target whose memory decays exponentially, the perturbation-error curves for different hidden dimensions all pass through a common point, and to the left of a positive stability radius the limiting curve stays continuous. A stable approximation exists.

en.caption: Figure 1. Perturbation error against perturbation strength beta for a linear target with exponentially decaying memory, across hidden dimensions m = 2 to 14. A positive stability radius exists (marked in red): to its left the limiting error curve stays continuous, so the target is stably approximable.

en.text: The inverse theorem: nonlinearity does not help

With these tools in place, the main theorem is a clean converse statement. If a target with decaying memory is stably approximated by nonlinear RNNs whose weight norms and perturbed memories stay uniformly controlled, then the target's memory must decay exponentially. The proof uses stability to drive the hidden-state derivatives toward zero and then invokes the Hartman-Grobman theorem to bound the eigenvalues of the recurrent matrices, forcing exponential decay. Nonlinearity, it turns out, does not lift the curse of memory; it inherits it.

The numerics tell the same story from the other side. When the target has only polynomially decaying memory, the stability that Figure 1 enjoyed disappears. Instead of converging to a continuous limiting curve, the perturbation-error curves for different hidden dimensions keep intersecting further and further to the left as the dimension grows, so no positive stability radius survives. Figure 2 shows this for a nonlinear tanh RNN, and it matches the linear case exactly.

en.caption: Figure 2. A nonlinear tanh RNN approximating a target with polynomially decaying memory (fit at 1000 epochs), for hidden dimensions m = 4 to 64. The curves keep crossing further left as m grows, so there is no positive stability radius: the target cannot be stably approximated.

en.text: The most direct evidence comes from a filtering experiment. The authors build several randomly initialized RNNs as teacher models with a large hidden dimension of m = 256, then approximate each with a series of student RNNs and numerically test whether the approximation is stable. Keeping only the teachers that are both approximable and stable leaves exactly one kind of survivor: teachers whose memory function decays exponentially. Figure 3 shows the stability test on the left and one surviving teacher's exponentially decaying memory on the right.

en.caption: Figure 3. Filtering random teacher RNNs (hidden dimension m = 256) by stability. Left: the perturbation error of student approximations across m = 4 to 64. Right: the memory function of a surviving teacher, which decays exponentially. Only exponential-memory teachers pass the stability filter.

en.text: The cure: stable reparameterization

If the problem is that ordinary training pushes the recurrent weight into regions where small perturbations blow up, the fix is to reparameterize so that every reachable weight is already stable. The authors replace the recurrent weight matrix with a continuous map that always lands in the set of matrices with negative real-part eigenvalues, for example an exponential map or a softplus map. The network can still push its eigenvalues toward the edge of stability to capture more memory, but it can no longer cross the edge, so the approximation stays continuous under perturbation.

Figure 4 confirms the recovery on the synthetic side. Applying exponential and softplus reparameterizations to a linear RNN approximating a polynomial-decay target restores the continuous limiting curve that was missing in Figure 2, exactly what the theory predicts a stable parameterization should do.

en.caption: Figure 4. The same polynomial-decay target as before, now approximated by a linear RNN with exponential and softplus reparameterization, across m = 2 to 14. The limiting curve is continuous again: stability, and with it approximability, is restored.

en.text: Does it help in practice? MNIST

The payoff is not only theoretical. On MNIST image classification, trained for 10 epochs from identical weight initializations and averaged over 3 repeats, the three stable reparameterizations all beat the direct, unstable parameterization that uses the recurrent weight as-is. Softplus reaches the best test accuracy, and because reparameterization does not change the model's inherent capacity, the improvement is an optimization and stability effect rather than a capacity change.

en.caption: Table 1. Test loss and accuracy of different recurrent-weight parameterizations on MNIST (10 epochs, averaged over 3 repeats). The stable maps all outperform the direct, unstable baseline.

en.text: The gap is modest but consistent: softplus lands at 71.36% against 68.47% for the unstable baseline, a gain of nearly 3 points, with exp and inverse also above 70%. The synthetic experiments sharpen the same point about difficulty. Exponential-memory targets are fit in roughly 10 epochs, whereas polynomial-memory targets need on the order of 1000 epochs and still fail the stability test.
Takeaway

The one-line version is this. No matter how you train them, plain nonlinear RNNs can only stably approximate sequence relationships whose memory fades exponentially, so their well-known struggle with long-term dependencies is a property of the architecture, not merely of the optimizer. That is the honest boundary of the negative result. The constructive half is that the same analysis names the cure: reparameterizing the recurrent weights with a stable map such as exponential or softplus keeps the eigenvalues near the edge of stability without crossing it, provably relaxing the curse of memory and, on a real task like MNIST, training faster and generalizing a little better.

Beyond RNNs, the two tools introduced here, a numerically queryable memory function and a perturbation-based notion of stable approximation, are general enough to extend toward gated architectures like GRU and LSTM. That gives practitioners a principled way to reason in advance about which sequence relationships a given recurrent model can and cannot hope to learn.

zh.text: 面对序列数据，比如时间序列、语音、文本、情感，循环神经网络（Recurrent Neural Network，RNN）往往是我们最先想到的基础模型。但它也有一个反复出现的短板：当输出依赖于很久之前发生的事情时，普通 RNN 常常会“断线”。对此，人们通常给出的是一个优化层面的解释，即梯度在沿着许多时间步反向传播时会消失或爆炸，让长距离依赖变得难以训练。
但这个解释回避了一个更尖锐的问题：RNN 在长期记忆上的困难，究竟只是一个可以靠更好的优化器修复的训练假象，还是模型本身能表示什么这件事上的结构性限制？两种诊断对应着完全不同的应对方式，而要把它们区分开，需要的是逼近理论（approximation theory）的视角，而不是优化的视角。

这篇 ICLR 2024 的论文为非线性 RNN 给出了答案。它证明了一个逆向（inverse，即 Bernstein 型）逼近定理：如果一个非线性 RNN 能够稳定地逼近某个目标序列关系，那么这个目标的记忆必然随时间指数衰减。换句话说，长期依赖上的困难是写进 RNN 假设空间里的，而不只是优化器的问题。更进一步，同一套分析还指向了一剂解药，即对循环权重做一种稳定重参数化（stable reparameterization），它在理论和实验上都能缓解这一限制。
作者：Zhong Li（微软亚洲研究院），Shida Wang、Qianxiao Li（新加坡国立大学；Institute for Functional Intelligent Materials）。
论文：https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.19190
逼近理论的两个方向
逼近理论提供了两类互补的陈述。正向（forward，即 Jackson 型）定理告诉你：对一个足够光滑的目标，模型能逼近到多好。逆向（inverse，即 Bernstein 型）定理则反过来走：先假设一个目标可以被高效逼近，再反推这个目标本身必须具备什么样的正则性。机器学习里的逼近结果大多是正向定理，这也是它们很少能揭示某种结构真正天花板的原因；而逆向定理，恰恰是干这件事的工具。

在此之前已有一个先例。早先的工作针对线性 RNN 证明了一个 Bernstein 型结果：线性 RNN 能高效逼近的任何线性目标，其记忆都必须指数衰减，这一现象被称为“记忆诅咒”（curse of memory）。真正悬而未决、也更迫切的问题是：非线性能不能打破这个诅咒？非线性大幅提升了模型容量，直觉上，更强的模型应当能记住更多过去的信息。这篇论文要问的，正是这个直觉在严格的逆向定理面前能否站得住。
两件工具：记忆函数与稳定逼近
整套分析立足于两个要素。第一个是记忆函数（memory function），它把线性情形下的定义推广到了任意的非线性泛函序列。它用 Heaviside 阶跃输入去探测模型，通过响应对时间的导数，度量时刻 t 的输出仍然对输入有多强的依赖。关键在于，这个记忆函数不只是一个抽象定义，它可以从训练好的模型中被数值地查询出来，于是我们真的能把一个网络记忆的衰减方式画成曲线。

第二个要素是稳定逼近（stable approximation）的概念。基于梯度的训练要想奏效，参数的小改动就必须只带来模型的小改动。为此，作者把隐藏维度为 m 时的扰动误差（perturbation error）定义为：当参数在半径为 beta 的球内被扰动时，输出误差的最坏情况值。如果这个扰动误差在某个正半径以内始终连续，就称该目标被稳定逼近，这个半径被称为稳定半径。这是一个温和、且对优化友好的要求，也是整个论证的枢纽。
图 1 把“好”的情形具体化了。对一个记忆指数衰减的目标，不同隐藏维度对应的扰动误差曲线会穿过同一个公共点，而在一个正稳定半径的左侧，极限曲线保持连续。也就是说，稳定逼近是存在的。

zh.caption: 图1 隐藏维度 m = 2 到 14 时，扰动误差随扰动强度 beta 的变化，目标为记忆指数衰减的线性泛函。存在一个正的稳定半径（红色标注）：在其左侧极限误差曲线保持连续，因此该目标可被稳定逼近。

zh.text: 逆向定理：非线性并没有帮上忙
有了这两件工具，主定理就是一个干净的逆命题：如果一个记忆衰减的目标，能被权重范数与扰动后记忆都被一致控制住的非线性 RNN 稳定逼近，那么这个目标的记忆必然指数衰减。证明利用稳定性把隐藏状态的导数逼向零，再借助 Hartman-Grobman 定理去约束循环矩阵的特征值，从而强制出指数衰减。结果是：非线性并没有解除记忆诅咒，而是继承了它。
数值实验从另一面讲了同样的故事。当目标的记忆只是多项式衰减时，图 1 中那种稳定性就消失了。不同隐藏维度的扰动误差曲线不再收敛到一条连续的极限曲线，而是随着维度增大，交点不断向左移动，于是没有任何正的稳定半径能够存活下来。图 2 用一个非线性 tanh RNN 展示了这一点，它与线性情形如出一辙。

zh.caption: 图2 非线性 tanh RNN 逼近一个记忆多项式衰减的目标（在 1000 个 epoch 时拟合完成），隐藏维度 m = 4 到 64。随着 m 增大，曲线交点持续向左移动，不存在正的稳定半径：该目标无法被稳定逼近。

zh.text: 最直接的证据来自一个筛选实验。作者构造了若干个随机初始化、隐藏维度很大（m = 256）的 RNN 作为教师模型，再用一系列学生 RNN 去逼近每一个教师，并数值检验这个逼近是否稳定。只保留那些既可被逼近、逼近又稳定的教师之后，剩下的恰好只有一类：记忆函数指数衰减的教师。图 3 左侧是稳定性检验，右侧是一个存活教师指数衰减的记忆函数。

zh.caption: 图3 按稳定性筛选随机教师 RNN（隐藏维度 m = 256）。左：学生逼近在 m = 4 到 64 时的扰动误差。右：一个存活教师的记忆函数，呈指数衰减。只有记忆指数衰减的教师能通过稳定性筛选。

zh.text: 解药：稳定重参数化
既然问题在于普通训练会把循环权重推到“小扰动就会放大”的区域，那么解法就是重新参数化，让所有可达到的权重从一开始就是稳定的。作者用一个连续映射来替换循环权重矩阵，这个映射的取值始终落在“特征值实部为负”的矩阵集合里，例如指数映射或 softplus 映射。网络仍然可以把特征值推向稳定的边缘以捕捉更多记忆，但再也无法越过这条边，于是逼近在扰动下保持连续。
图 4 在合成数据上确认了这种恢复。对一个多项式衰减的目标，用指数和 softplus 重参数化的线性 RNN 去逼近，图 2 中缺失的连续极限曲线又回来了，这正是理论预测稳定参数化应当带来的效果。

zh.caption: 图4 仍是前面那个多项式衰减目标，改由带指数和 softplus 重参数化的线性 RNN 逼近，隐藏维度 m = 2 到 14。极限曲线重新变得连续：稳定性，连同可逼近性，都被恢复了。

zh.text: 在真实任务上有用吗：MNIST
这套方法的回报并不只停留在理论上。在 MNIST 图像分类任务上，从完全相同的权重初始化出发、训练 10 个 epoch、并对 3 次重复取平均后，三种稳定重参数化都胜过了“直接”（direct）这种把循环权重原样使用的不稳定参数化。其中 softplus 取得了最好的测试准确率；而由于重参数化并不改变模型固有的容量，这一提升反映的是优化与稳定性上的收益，而非容量的变化。

zh.caption: 表1 不同循环权重参数化方式在 MNIST 上的测试损失与准确率（训练 10 个 epoch，对 3 次重复取平均）。三种稳定映射都优于直接的不稳定基线。

zh.text: 差距不大但很一致：softplus 达到 71.36%，而不稳定基线为 68.47%，提升接近 3 个百分点，exp 与 inverse 也都在 70% 以上。合成实验则把关于“难度”的这一点说得更透彻：记忆指数衰减的目标大约 10 个 epoch 就能拟合，而记忆多项式衰减的目标需要约 1000 个 epoch，并且即便如此依然通不过稳定性检验。
小结

一句话总结：无论你怎么训练，普通的非线性 RNN 只能稳定逼近那些记忆随时间指数衰减的序列关系，因此它们在长期依赖上众所周知的挣扎，是架构本身的性质，而不仅仅是优化器的问题。这是这个否定性结论诚实的边界。而它建设性的一半在于，同一套分析给出了解药：用指数或 softplus 这样的稳定映射去重参数化循环权重，可以让特征值贴近稳定的边缘却不越界，从而在理论上缓解记忆诅咒，并在 MNIST 这样的真实任务上训练更快、泛化也略好。
而且，这里引入的两件工具，即可被数值查询的记忆函数，以及基于扰动的稳定逼近概念，足够通用，能够向 GRU、LSTM 这类门控架构延伸，为“某个循环模型到底能学到、又学不到哪些序列关系”提供一条有原则的分析路径。

逼近理论提供了两类互补的陈述。正向（forward，即 Jackson 型）定理告诉你：对一个足够光滑的目标，模型能逼近到多好。逆向（inverse，即 Bernstein 型）定理则反过来走：先假设一个目标可以被高效逼近，再反推这个目标本身必须具备什么样的正则性。机器学习里的逼近结果大多是正向定理，这也是它们很少能揭示某种结构真正天花板的原因；而逆向定理，恰恰是干这件事的工具。

在此之前已有一个先例。早先的工作针对线性 RNN 证明了一个 Bernstein 型结果：线性 RNN 能高效逼近的任何线性目标，其记忆都必须指数衰减，这一现象被称为“记忆诅咒”（curse of memory）。真正悬而未决、也更迫切的问题是：非线性能不能打破这个诅咒？非线性大幅提升了模型容量，直觉上，更强的模型应当能记住更多过去的信息。这篇论文要问的，正是这个直觉在严格的逆向定理面前能否站得住。

zh.title: ICLR 2024 | 非线性 RNN 为什么记不住长期依赖，又该如何松绑
zh.subtitle: 一个逆向逼近定理证明：非线性 RNN 能够稳定学到的目标，其记忆必然随时间指数衰减；而一种有原则的稳定重参数化可以缓解这一限制。微软亚洲研究院与新加坡国立大学的工作。

en.text: Two tools: a memory function and stable approximation

The analysis rests on two ingredients. The first is a memory function generalized from the linear setting to arbitrary nonlinear functional sequences. It probes the model with Heaviside step inputs and measures how strongly the output at time t still responds to the input, through the derivative of that response. Crucially, this memory function is not just an abstract definition: it can be numerically queried from a trained model, so you can actually plot how a network's memory decays.

The second ingredient is a notion of stable approximation. Gradient-based training only works if small changes to the parameters cause small changes to the model, so the authors define the perturbation error at hidden dimension m as the worst-case output error when the parameters are perturbed within a ball of radius beta. A target is stably approximated if that perturbation error stays continuous up to some positive radius, called the stability radius. This is a mild, optimization-friendly requirement, and it is the hinge of the whole argument.

Figure 1 makes the good case concrete. For a target whose memory decays exponentially, the perturbation-error curves for different hidden dimensions all pass through a common point, and to the left of a positive stability radius the limiting curve stays continuous. A stable approximation exists.

en.caption: Figure 1. Perturbation error against perturbation strength beta for a linear target with exponentially decaying memory, across hidden dimensions m = 2 to 14. A positive stability radius exists (marked in red): to its left the limiting error curve stays continuous, so the target is stably approximable.

zh.text: 两件工具：记忆函数与稳定逼近
整套分析立足于两个要素。第一个是记忆函数（memory function），它把线性情形下的定义推广到了任意的非线性泛函序列。它用 Heaviside 阶跃输入去探测模型，通过响应对时间的导数，度量时刻 t 的输出仍然对输入有多强的依赖。关键在于，这个记忆函数不只是一个抽象定义，它可以从训练好的模型中被数值地查询出来，于是我们真的能把一个网络记忆的衰减方式画成曲线。

第二个要素是稳定逼近（stable approximation）的概念。基于梯度的训练要想奏效，参数的小改动就必须只带来模型的小改动。为此，作者把隐藏维度为 m 时的扰动误差（perturbation error）定义为：当参数在半径为 beta 的球内被扰动时，输出误差的最坏情况值。如果这个扰动误差在某个正半径以内始终连续，就称该目标被稳定逼近，这个半径被称为稳定半径。这是一个温和、且对优化友好的要求，也是整个论证的枢纽。
图 1 把“好”的情形具体化了。对一个记忆指数衰减的目标，不同隐藏维度对应的扰动误差曲线会穿过同一个公共点，而在一个正稳定半径的左侧，极限曲线保持连续。也就是说，稳定逼近是存在的。

zh.caption: 图1 隐藏维度 m = 2 到 14 时，扰动误差随扰动强度 beta 的变化，目标为记忆指数衰减的线性泛函。存在一个正的稳定半径（红色标注）：在其左侧极限误差曲线保持连续，因此该目标可被稳定逼近。

zh.subtitle: 一个逆向逼近定理证明：非线性 RNN 能够稳定学到的目标，其记忆必然随时间指数衰减；而一种有原则的稳定重参数化可以缓解这一限制。微软亚洲研究院与新加坡国立大学的工作。

en.caption: Figure 1. Perturbation error against perturbation strength beta for a linear target with exponentially decaying memory, across hidden dimensions m = 2 to 14. A positive stability radius exists (marked in red): to its left the limiting error curve stays continuous, so the target is stably approximable.

en.text: Takeaway

The one-line version is this. No matter how you train them, plain nonlinear RNNs can only stably approximate sequence relationships whose memory fades exponentially, so their well-known struggle with long-term dependencies is a property of the architecture, not merely of the optimizer. That is the honest boundary of the negative result. The constructive half is that the same analysis names the cure: reparameterizing the recurrent weights with a stable map such as exponential or softplus keeps the eigenvalues near the edge of stability without crossing it, provably relaxing the curse of memory and, on a real task like MNIST, training faster and generalizing a little better.

Beyond RNNs, the two tools introduced here, a numerically queryable memory function and a perturbation-based notion of stable approximation, are general enough to extend toward gated architectures like GRU and LSTM. That gives practitioners a principled way to reason in advance about which sequence relationships a given recurrent model can and cannot hope to learn.

zh.caption: 图1 隐藏维度 m = 2 到 14 时，扰动误差随扰动强度 beta 的变化，目标为记忆指数衰减的线性泛函。存在一个正的稳定半径（红色标注）：在其左侧极限误差曲线保持连续，因此该目标可被稳定逼近。

zh.text: 在真实任务上有用吗：MNIST
这套方法的回报并不只停留在理论上。在 MNIST 图像分类任务上，从完全相同的权重初始化出发、训练 10 个 epoch、并对 3 次重复取平均后，三种稳定重参数化都胜过了“直接”（direct）这种把循环权重原样使用的不稳定参数化。其中 softplus 取得了最好的测试准确率；而由于重参数化并不改变模型固有的容量，这一提升反映的是优化与稳定性上的收益，而非容量的变化。

zh.caption: 表1 不同循环权重参数化方式在 MNIST 上的测试损失与准确率（训练 10 个 epoch，对 3 次重复取平均）。三种稳定映射都优于直接的不稳定基线。

zh.text: 差距不大但很一致：softplus 达到 71.36%，而不稳定基线为 68.47%，提升接近 3 个百分点，exp 与 inverse 也都在 70% 以上。合成实验则把关于“难度”的这一点说得更透彻：记忆指数衰减的目标大约 10 个 epoch 就能拟合，而记忆多项式衰减的目标需要约 1000 个 epoch，并且即便如此依然通不过稳定性检验。

en.text: The cure: stable reparameterization

If the problem is that ordinary training pushes the recurrent weight into regions where small perturbations blow up, the fix is to reparameterize so that every reachable weight is already stable. The authors replace the recurrent weight matrix with a continuous map that always lands in the set of matrices with negative real-part eigenvalues, for example an exponential map or a softplus map. The network can still push its eigenvalues toward the edge of stability to capture more memory, but it can no longer cross the edge, so the approximation stays continuous under perturbation.

Figure 4 confirms the recovery on the synthetic side. Applying exponential and softplus reparameterizations to a linear RNN approximating a polynomial-decay target restores the continuous limiting curve that was missing in Figure 2, exactly what the theory predicts a stable parameterization should do.

en.caption: Figure 4. The same polynomial-decay target as before, now approximated by a linear RNN with exponential and softplus reparameterization, across m = 2 to 14. The limiting curve is continuous again: stability, and with it approximability, is restored.

zh.text: 解药：稳定重参数化
既然问题在于普通训练会把循环权重推到“小扰动就会放大”的区域，那么解法就是重新参数化，让所有可达到的权重从一开始就是稳定的。作者用一个连续映射来替换循环权重矩阵，这个映射的取值始终落在“特征值实部为负”的矩阵集合里，例如指数映射或 softplus 映射。网络仍然可以把特征值推向稳定的边缘以捕捉更多记忆，但再也无法越过这条边，于是逼近在扰动下保持连续。
图 4 在合成数据上确认了这种恢复。对一个多项式衰减的目标，用指数和 softplus 重参数化的线性 RNN 去逼近，图 2 中缺失的连续极限曲线又回来了，这正是理论预测稳定参数化应当带来的效果。

zh.caption: 图4 仍是前面那个多项式衰减目标，改由带指数和 softplus 重参数化的线性 RNN 逼近，隐藏维度 m = 2 到 14。极限曲线重新变得连续：稳定性，连同可逼近性，都被恢复了。

en.text: Two directions in approximation theory

Approximation theory offers two complementary kinds of statement. A forward, or Jackson-type, theorem tells you how well a model can approximate a target that is sufficiently regular. On MNIST image classification, trained for 10 epochs from identical weight initializations and averaged over 3 repeats, the three stable reparameterizations all beat the direct, unstable parameterization that uses the recurrent weight as-is. Softplus reaches the best test accuracy, and because reparameterization does not change the model's inherent capacity, the improvement is an optimization and stability effect rather than a capacity change.

en.text: The gap is modest but consistent: softplus lands at 71.36% against 68.47% for the unstable baseline, a gain of nearly 3 points, with exp and inverse also above 70%. en.subtitle: An inverse approximation theorem shows that any target a nonlinear RNN can stably learn must have exponentially fading memory, and a principled stable reparameterization relaxes the limit. Work by Microsoft Research Asia and the National University of Singapore.

zh.title: ICLR 2024 | 非线性 RNN 为什么记不住长期依赖，又该如何松绑
zh.subtitle: 一个逆向逼近定理证明：非线性 RNN 能够稳定学到的目标，其记忆必然随时间指数衰减；而一种有原则的稳定重参数化可以缓解这一限制。微软亚洲研究院与新加坡国立大学的工作。

en.caption: Figure 1. Perturbation error against perturbation strength beta for a linear target with exponentially decaying memory, across hidden dimensions m = 2 to 14. A positive stability radius exists (marked in red): to its left the limiting error curve stays continuous, so the target is stably approximable.

en.text: Recurrent neural networks are one of the most basic tools we reach for when data arrives as a sequence: time series, speech, text, sentiment. They are also famous for one recurring disappointment. When the signal depends on something that happened far in the past, plain RNNs tend to lose the thread. The usual explanation is an optimization story: gradients that vanish or explode as they are propagated back through many time steps, making long-range dependencies hard to train.

But that explanation leaves a sharper question unanswered. Is the trouble with long-term memory merely a training artifact that a better optimizer might fix, or is it a structural limit of what an RNN can represent at all? The two diagnoses call for very different responses, and telling them apart requires an approximation-theoretic lens rather than an optimization one.

This ICLR 2024 paper settles the question for nonlinear RNNs. It proves an inverse, or Bernstein-type, approximation theorem: if a nonlinear RNN can stably approximate a target sequence relationship, then that target's memory must decay exponentially in time. In other words, the difficulty with long-term dependencies is baked into the RNN hypothesis space, not just the optimizer. The same analysis then points to a cure, a stable reparameterization of the recurrent weights that provably and empirically relaxes the limit.
Authors: Zhong Li (Microsoft Research Asia), Shida Wang and Qianxiao Li (National University of Singapore; Institute for Functional Intelligent Materials).
Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.19190

zh.caption: 图1 隐藏维度 m = 2 到 14 时，扰动误差随扰动强度 beta 的变化，目标为记忆指数衰减的线性泛函。存在一个正的稳定半径（红色标注）：在其左侧极限误差曲线保持连续，因此该目标可被稳定逼近。

zh.text: 面对序列数据，比如时间序列、语音、文本、情感，循环神经网络（Recurrent Neural Network，RNN）往往是我们最先想到的基础模型。但它也有一个反复出现的短板：当输出依赖于很久之前发生的事情时，普通 RNN 常常会“断线”。对此，人们通常给出的是一个优化层面的解释，即梯度在沿着许多时间步反向传播时会消失或爆炸，让长距离依赖变得难以训练。
但这个解释回避了一个更尖锐的问题：RNN 在长期记忆上的困难，究竟只是一个可以靠更好的优化器修复的训练假象，还是模型本身能表示什么这件事上的结构性限制？两种诊断对应着完全不同的应对方式，而要把它们区分开，需要的是逼近理论（approximation theory）的视角，而不是优化的视角。

这篇 ICLR 2024 的论文为非线性 RNN 给出了答案。它证明了一个逆向（inverse，即 Bernstein 型）逼近定理：如果一个非线性 RNN 能够稳定地逼近某个目标序列关系，那么这个目标的记忆必然随时间指数衰减。换句话说，长期依赖上的困难是写进 RNN 假设空间里的，而不只是优化器的问题。更进一步，同一套分析还指向了一剂解药，即对循环权重做一种稳定重参数化（stable reparameterization），它在理论和实验上都能缓解这一限制。
作者：Zhong Li（微软亚洲研究院），Shida Wang、Qianxiao Li（新加坡国立大学；Institute for Functional Intelligent Materials）。
论文：https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.19190

zh.text: 面对序列数据，比如时间序列、语音、文本、情感，循环神经网络（Recurrent Neural Network，RNN）往往是我们最先想到的基础模型。但它也有一个反复出现的短板：当输出依赖于很久之前发生的事情时，普通 RNN 常常会“断线”。对此，人们通常给出的是一个优化层面的解释，即梯度在沿着许多时间步反向传播时会消失或爆炸，让长距离依赖变得难以训练。
但这个解释回避了一个更尖锐的问题：RNN 在长期记忆上的困难，究竟只是一个可以靠更好的优化器修复的训练假象，还是模型本身能表示什么这件事上的结构性限制？两种诊断对应着完全不同的应对方式，而要把它们区分开，需要的是逼近理论（approximation theory）的视角，而不是优化的视角。

这篇 ICLR 2024 的论文为非线性 RNN 给出了答案。它证明了一个逆向（inverse，即 Bernstein 型）逼近定理：如果一个非线性 RNN 能够稳定地逼近某个目标序列关系，那么这个目标的记忆必然随时间指数衰减。换句话说，长期依赖上的困难是写进 RNN 假设空间里的，而不只是优化器的问题。更进一步，同一套分析还指向了一剂解药，即对循环权重做一种稳定重参数化（stable reparameterization），它在理论和实验上都能缓解这一限制。
作者：Zhong Li（微软亚洲研究院），Shida Wang、Qianxiao Li（新加坡国立大学；Institute for Functional Intelligent Materials）。
论文：https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.19190

en.title: ICLR 2024 | Why Nonlinear RNNs Struggle to Remember, and How to Loosen the Limit
en.subtitle: An inverse approximation theorem shows that any target a nonlinear RNN can stably learn must have exponentially fading memory, and a principled stable reparameterization relaxes the limit. Work by Microsoft Research Asia and the National University of Singapore.

zh.title: ICLR 2024 | 非线性 RNN 为什么记不住长期依赖，又该如何松绑
zh.subtitle: 一个逆向逼近定理证明：非线性 RNN 能够稳定学到的目标，其记忆必然随时间指数衰减；而一种有原则的稳定重参数化可以缓解这一限制。微软亚洲研究院与新加坡国立大学的工作。

en.caption: Figure 1. Perturbation error against perturbation strength beta for a linear target with exponentially decaying memory, across hidden dimensions m = 2 to 14. A positive stability radius exists (marked in red): to its left the limiting error curve stays continuous, so the target is stably approximable.

en.text: Does it help in practice? MNIST

The payoff is not only theoretical. On MNIST image classification, trained for 10 epochs from identical weight initializations and averaged over 3 repeats, the three stable reparameterizations all beat the direct, unstable parameterization that uses the recurrent weight as-is. Softplus reaches the best test accuracy, and because reparameterization does not change the model's inherent capacity, the improvement is an optimization and stability effect rather than a capacity change.

en.caption: Table 1. Test loss and accuracy of different recurrent-weight parameterizations on MNIST (10 epochs, averaged over 3 repeats). The stable maps all outperform the direct, unstable baseline.

en.text: The gap is modest but consistent: softplus lands at 71.36% against 68.47% for the unstable baseline, a gain of nearly 3 points, with exp and inverse also above 70%. The synthetic experiments sharpen the same point about difficulty. Exponential-memory targets are fit in roughly 10 epochs, whereas polynomial-memory targets need on the order of 1000 epochs and still fail the stability test.
Takeaway

The one-line version is this. No matter how you train them, plain nonlinear RNNs can only stably approximate sequence relationships whose memory fades exponentially, so their well-known struggle with long-term dependencies is a property of the architecture, not merely of the optimizer. That is the honest boundary of the negative result. The constructive half is that the same analysis names the cure: reparameterizing the recurrent weights with a stable map such as exponential or softplus keeps the eigenvalues near the edge of stability without crossing it, provably relaxing the curse of memory and, on a real task like MNIST, training faster and generalizing a little better.

Beyond RNNs, the two tools introduced here, a numerically queryable memory function and a perturbation-based notion of stable approximation, are general enough to extend toward gated architectures like GRU and LSTM. That gives practitioners a principled way to reason in advance about which sequence relationships a given recurrent model can and cannot hope to learn.

zh.text: 小结

一句话总结：无论你怎么训练，普通的非线性 RNN 只能稳定逼近那些记忆随时间指数衰减的序列关系，因此它们在长期依赖上众所周知的挣扎，是架构本身的性质，而不仅仅是优化器的问题。这是这个否定性结论诚实的边界。而它建设性的一半在于，同一套分析给出了解药：用指数或 softplus 这样的稳定映射去重参数化循环权重，可以让特征值贴近稳定的边缘却不越界，从而在理论上缓解记忆诅咒，并在 MNIST 这样的真实任务上训练更快、泛化也略好。
而且，这里引入的两件工具，即可被数值查询的记忆函数，以及基于扰动的稳定逼近概念，足够通用，能够向 GRU、LSTM 这类门控架构延伸，为“某个循环模型到底能学到、又学不到哪些序列关系”提供一条有原则的分析路径。
